subject.name: Ethereum Name Service (ENS)
subject.one_line: ENS gives people and apps readable names for addresses and other records on Ethereum.

summary.text: ENS gives people readable names that can point to Ethereum addresses and other records.
Use the ENS App to find and register an available name or manage a name you already hold.
ENS lists a one-year fee of $8 for names with at least five characters, with higher prices for shorter names and a separate network fee.
The project says the name app can swap Ethereum’s currency into digital dollars to pay for a name.
The project says name fees go to the community that runs ENS, and payments on the new version reach its investment fund.
The project says its separate voting token lets holders give their votes to someone who can act for them.
Nick Johnson started ENS, and a community of token holders now governs its rules and treasury.
ENS announced that its new system went live, while its deployment guide still describes the switch as pending.

differs.why: The homepage and dated launch notice say version 2 went live. The deployment guide still describes version 1 as handling new registrations until cutover. The governor and a later version 2 registration show that activation and new registration occurred.

open_questions: When will ENS reconcile the deployment guide’s launch wording with the October 27 cutover?
What will the registrar quote for a visitor’s particular name, term and payment token at checkout?
What are the current counts of live name tokens by version and minted ENSC cards? The collectible contract did not return a totalSupply reading.
What is the complete current set of payment tokens? The two public calls check USDC and DAI individually.
Which other accounts currently hold administrative or upgrade roles on the version 2 contracts?
notes: F1 was the only prior file supplied. All 19 earlier lines are carried, including the three older readings in proof history, and F1 supplied no changes file or reconsider list. The main marker follows the requested Registry address and its role in version 1 lookups. The version 2 root registry, registrar and lookup proxy are listed separately. Proofs use pinned Ethereum block numbers. Replay may require a history-serving archive node after pruning. The registry deployment sender was checked against the chain transaction and the created address against the indexed receipt in Blockscout, after Etherscan returned HTTP 403. Channel strength uses direct name records where available. The documentation is weak because its deployment page publishes the supplied address. The other first-party sites and YouTube account are listed in ENS support, which is separate evidence from an on-chain tie. The token box lists transferable name token families as well as the governance token and commemorative collection. The name families have descriptive labels because these contracts did not return token symbols. USDC and DAI are payment assets issued elsewhere. Individual name prices and network fees vary.
